voice.refText: You wake up and discover you can pause time. 10 seconds once a day. At first, you use it for dumb things. You catch your falling coffee. You dodge your boss in the hallway.

Old woman.describe: A warm, clear female alto: a kind woman in her seventies on a metro platform, a grandmother. Gentle and unhurried, a smile in the voice, crisp clear diction, every word distinct, standard English with no slang.

Min-jun.describe: A bright, light male tenor-baritone: a boy of eighteen, your best friend since you were twelve. Quick, warm and easy, a grin in every word, crisp clear diction, every word distinct, casual modern English.

Clerk.describe: A sleepy male baritone: a convenience-store clerk in his twenties on the night shift. Slow, polite and flat, clear diction under the tiredness.

Ji-yoon.describe: A warm female mezzo: a woman of twenty-four, your older sister, tired from night shifts. Soft and low, gentle and teasing, clear diction, she speaks close and slowly, as if she has all the time in the world for you.

Tae-ho.describe: A flat, cool male baritone: a boy of eighteen, the class rival. Bored and clipped, half a smirk, never looks up from what he is doing, short words.

Teacher.describe: A crisp female alto: a maths teacher in her forties. Precise and dry, one word at a time, kind underneath but never says so.

Kid.describe: A high, bright child's voice, about ten years old. Quick, natural and lively.

lines.text: Old woman: Oh, congratulations! Your family must be so proud.
lines.say: [warm, delighted, clear and unhurried, a grandmother's smile] Oh, congratulations! Your family must be so proud.
lines.speaker: Old woman

lines.text: That's your scholarship letter. You made the cut. And a card just opened over a stranger, with a number only you can see.
lines.say: [low, quick, amazed, keeping a secret] That's your scholarship letter. You made the cut. And a card just opened over a stranger, with a number only you can see.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: So what if every piece of good news showed you who wants you to fail? You tell nobody all day. Because your best friend hears everything first. He always has.
lines.say: [curious, leaning in on the question, then warm and fond] So what if every piece of good news showed you who wants you to fail? You tell nobody all day. Because your best friend hears everything first. He always has.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Ten at night. Extra classes finally let out. And waiting at the bottom of the steps, like every night: your best friend.
lines.say: [warm, unhurried, a lift on the last three words] Ten at night. Extra classes finally let out. And waiting at the bottom of the steps, like every night: your best friend.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Because that's your best friend. And that's minus eighty-four.
lines.say: [flat, hurt held in, a beat before the number] Because that's your best friend. And that's minus eighty-four.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Min-jun: Knew it. Knew it.
lines.say: [delighted, delighted, laughing, clear] Knew it. Knew it.
lines.speaker: Min-jun

lines.text: Sixty seconds. The card folds shut. His arm stays. So does the number.
lines.say: [low, steady, the last sentence landing] Sixty seconds. The card folds shut. His arm stays. So does the number.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: The rule, once. Say your good news out loud, to someone's face, and a card opens over their head. For sixty seconds, it shows how your news lands with them.
lines.say: [clear, slow, exact, letting each part land] The rule, once. Say your good news out loud, to someone's face, and a card opens over their head. For sixty seconds, it shows how your news lands with them.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Plus one hundred means pure joy for you. Minus one hundred means they want you to fail.
lines.say: [plain, a shade colder on the second half] Plus one hundred means pure joy for you. Minus one hundred means they want you to fail.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: And it never tells you why.
lines.say: [quiet, slow, a warning] And it never tells you why.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Min-jun: You want half?
lines.say: You want half?
lines.speaker: Min-jun

lines.text: Every night, one chocolate bar, two halves. You take yours. Tonight you watch him chew.
lines.say: [warm, then watchful on the last sentence] Every night, one chocolate bar, two halves. You take yours. Tonight you watch him chew.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: The only other face in the shop: the clerk.
lines.say: [amused, a small dare] The only other face in the shop: the clerk.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Clerk: Receipt?
lines.say: [bored, not looking up] Receipt?
lines.speaker: Clerk

lines.text: Zero. Grey. One click. The biggest news of your life, and you're a receipt.
lines.say: [deadpan, the joke landing dry] Zero. Grey. One click. The biggest news of your life, and you're a receipt.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: The cat on the crate. Nothing. Not even a card.
lines.say: [deadpan, slower] The cat on the crate. Nothing. Not even a card.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: So either a cat isn't a face, or a cat doesn't care. You'll never know.
lines.say: [amused, a shrug in the voice] So either a cat isn't a face, or a cat doesn't care. You'll never know.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Your phone. Your sister. Six years of night shifts at a warehouse to pay for that classroom. You tell her.
lines.say: [warm, a weight on six years, then quick on the last three words] Your phone. Your sister. Six years of night shifts at a warehouse to pay for that classroom. You tell her.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Ji-yoon: Say it again.
lines.say: Say it again.
lines.speaker: Ji-yoon

lines.text: You do. You're grinning into a phone. And nothing opens over a phone.
lines.say: [fond, then the last sentence dropped flat] You do. You're grinning into a phone. And nothing opens over a phone.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: So you've read your best friend. And her number, you still don't have.
lines.say: [quiet, leaning in, a question left hanging] So you've read your best friend. And her number, you still don't have.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Next morning. You've worked it out. Red is for enemies. So you go looking for one.
lines.say: [brisk, confident, a little mischievous] Next morning. You've worked it out. Red is for enemies. So you go looking for one.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: The rival. Trash-talks you every morning, two years running.
lines.say: [dry, relishing it] The rival. Trash-talks you every morning, two years running.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Tae-ho: Still here?
lines.say: [bored contempt, not looking] Still here?
lines.speaker: Tae-ho

lines.text: You hold up the letter.
lines.say: [a held breath, quick] You hold up the letter.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Minus six. He barely looks up.
lines.say: [surprised, flat, almost disappointed] Minus six. He barely looks up.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Tae-ho: Nice. Move.
lines.say: [indifferent, already past you] Nice. Move.
lines.speaker: Tae-ho

lines.text: Two years of trash talk: minus six. Your best friend: minus eighty-four. Whatever red means, the dangerous number is at the next desk.
lines.say: [dry, then low and certain on the last clause] Two years of trash talk: minus six. Your best friend: minus eighty-four. Whatever red means, the dangerous number is at the next desk.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Your maths teacher.
lines.say: [quick, a new try] Your maths teacher.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Teacher: Good.
lines.say: [clipped, warm underneath, eyes on the marking] Good.
lines.speaker: Teacher

lines.text: One word. And plus forty-one.
lines.say: [surprised, a small smile] One word. And plus forty-one.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: The mirror in the school toilets. Nothing opens. So a mirror isn't a face. Or the one card you can't see is yours.
lines.say: [curious, slower, the last sentence a little eerie] The mirror in the school toilets. Nothing opens. So a mirror isn't a face. Or the one card you can't see is yours.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Outside the station, a tour group. Eleven of them, following a flag. You say it to all eleven.
lines.say: [amused, building, quick] Outside the station, a tour group. Eleven of them, following a flag. You say it to all eleven.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Eleven cards. Eleven zeros, in a row, like a timetable.
lines.say: [deadpan, flat as the zeros] Eleven cards. Eleven zeros, in a row, like a timetable.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: The bus home. A little kid in a cap, feet swinging. You try him.
lines.say: [soft, amused, a last try of the day] The bus home. A little kid in a cap, feet swinging. You try him.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Kid: What did you win?
lines.say: [delighted, loud, six years old] What did you win?
lines.speaker: Kid

lines.text: Plus seventy-seven. The highest number of the day is a six-year-old who doesn't know what a scholarship is.
lines.say: [warm, surprised, a laugh under it] Plus seventy-seven. The highest number of the day is a six-year-old who doesn't know what a scholarship is.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: So a kid gives you everything, your enemy gives you nothing, and your best friend gives you minus eighty-four. Why?
lines.say: [puzzled, building, the question held] So a kid gives you everything, your enemy gives you nothing, and your best friend gives you minus eighty-four. Why?
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: We measure ourselves against people near our own level, not far above or below.
lines.say: [clear, calm, the fact plain] We measure ourselves against people near our own level, not far above or below.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: And envy picks someone who started where you did, in a thing that matters to you.
lines.say: [calm, a little slower, landing on you] And envy picks someone who started where you did, in a thing that matters to you.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: The kid isn't in the race. The rival is twenty places ahead and throws that line at everyone. Your best friend has the next desk, the same chocolate bar, the same exam.
lines.say: [steady, each item a step closer, the last three softer] The kid isn't in the race. The rival is twenty places ahead and throws that line at everyone. Your best friend has the next desk, the same chocolate bar, the same exam.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: But here's the problem. Problem one: the only people who can bleed at your news are the ones in your lane. The same race. The ones you'd miss.
lines.say: [leaning in, hushed, the last four words quiet] But here's the problem. Problem one: the only people who can bleed at your news are the ones in your lane. The same race. The ones you'd miss.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: So you ask him, on the academy steps.
lines.say: [quiet, a decision] So you ask him, on the academy steps.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Min-jun: What number?
lines.say: [baffled, laughing, looking up] What number?
lines.speaker: Min-jun

lines.text: Min-jun: Is it a bug? Get it off.
lines.say: [mock panic, laughing, swatting] Is it a bug? Get it off.
lines.speaker: Min-jun

lines.text: He can't see it. Nobody sees the cards but you.
lines.say: [flat, quiet, the laugh gone] He can't see it. Nobody sees the cards but you.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: And people don't like to admit being maliciously envious, even to themselves.
lines.say: [calm, careful, a fact said gently] And people don't like to admit being maliciously envious, even to themselves.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: So you have a number, and no one to ask. Not him. Not her. Not yet.
lines.say: [low, the last three words a hook] So you have a number, and no one to ask. Not him. Not her. Not yet.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Eleven. Home. The letter's already on the fridge, next to the jar where her paintbrushes have stood for six years.
lines.say: [tired, warm, slowing on the brushes] Eleven. Home. The letter's already on the fridge, next to the jar where her paintbrushes have stood for six years.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: She's in the doorway, pulling on her work vest. She doesn't turn round.
lines.say: [quiet, watching] She's in the doorway, pulling on her work vest. She doesn't turn round.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Ji-yoon: Say it again.
lines.say: [bright, teasing, tired but glad, down a phone line] Say it again.
lines.speaker: Ji-yoon

lines.text: You say it to her back. Nothing opens. A back is not a face.
lines.say: [soft, dry, a half-smile] You say it to her back. Nothing opens. A back is not a face.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: She laughs, and she's gone. Her number stays hidden. And before you risk seeing it, you test the rule on everyone else.
lines.say: [warm, then a shade of fear on risk, then brisk] She laughs, and she's gone. Her number stays hidden. And before you risk seeing it, you test the rule on everyone else.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Minus six for the rival. So maybe a bigger crowd will show you who really wants you to fail.
lines.say: [thinking aloud, a plan forming, a little gleeful] Minus six for the rival. So maybe a bigger crowd will show you who really wants you to fail.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: This one neighbourhood in Seoul has about 1,000 after-school academies.
lines.say: [clear, a touch of awe] This one neighbourhood in Seoul has about a thousand after-school academies.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: And Seoul lets them teach only until ten at night. Inspectors have patrolled the streets to make sure.
lines.say: [dry, exact] And Seoul lets them teach only until ten at night. Inspectors have patrolled the streets to make sure.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: So at ten, every door on the street opens at once. A thousand faces.
lines.say: [building, hushed on the last two words] So at ten, every door on the street opens at once. A thousand faces.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: You climb the academy steps and say it into the crowd.
lines.say: [a breath in, quick, the dare] You climb the academy steps and say it into the crowd.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: You asked a thousand strangers to prove your best friend was the exception. Instead, every red card points back to your class.
lines.say: [quiet, the floor tilting, slower on the last words] You asked a thousand strangers to prove your best friend was the exception. Instead, every red card points back to your class.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: One is your best friend. So who are the other two?
lines.say: [quiet, sharp, the question hanging] One is your best friend. So who are the other two?
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: The girl who borrows your calculator. Minus thirty. The boy you walked home with all of first year. Minus forty-four.
lines.say: [flat, each name a small blow] The girl who borrows your calculator. Minus thirty. The boy you walked home with all of first year. Minus forty-four.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: So. Minus means they want you to fail. And now you know exactly who to cut.
lines.say: [cold, certain, a wrong certainty] So. Minus means they want you to fail. And now you know exactly who to cut.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: The exam grades on a curve. In most subjects, only the top 4 per cent get the top grade.
lines.say: [clear, exact, the fact plain] The exam grades on a curve. In most subjects, only the top four per cent get the top grade.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: So you picture your class. A hundred of you. Four places. You're fourth. He's fifth.
lines.say: [quiet arithmetic, the last two sentences slow] So you picture your class. A hundred of you. Four places. You're fourth. He's fifth.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: So the card becomes a weapon.
lines.say: [low, hard] So the card becomes a weapon.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Two weeks. Each mock score, you stand up, say it out loud, and read the room.
lines.say: [brisk, a montage voice, a little ruthless] Two weeks. Each mock score, you stand up, say it out loud, and read the room.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Teacher: Sit down.
lines.say: [sharp, tired, not unkind] Sit down.
lines.speaker: Teacher

lines.text: Anyone who goes red: out of the group chat. No more past papers from the shared folder. No notes. No help.
lines.say: [clipped, cold, each cut a beat] Anyone who goes red: out of the group chat. No more past papers from the shared folder. No notes. No help.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Week one, three red. Week two, nine.
lines.say: [flat, counting, a chill on nine] Week one, three red. Week two, nine.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Tae-ho: What's with you?
lines.say: [puzzled, half a sneer, half concern] What's with you?
lines.speaker: Tae-ho

lines.text: Even the rival's noticed. And he's still minus six.
lines.say: [dry, a wince of a joke] Even the rival's noticed. And he's still minus six.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: And every night at the counter:
lines.say: [soft, a lead-in, slowing] And every night at the counter:
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Min-jun: You want half...?
lines.say: [hopeful, tentative, smaller than before, still clear] You want half?
lines.speaker: Min-jun

lines.text: The next night, you come in alone.
lines.say: [quiet, bare] The next night, you come in alone.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Clerk: Just you tonight?
lines.say: [mild, noticing for once] Just you tonight?
lines.speaker: Clerk

lines.text: You climb. Fourth. Third. Second.
lines.say: [steady, each step higher and colder] You climb. Fourth. Third. Second.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: But the higher you go, the redder the room.
lines.say: [low, the turn of a screw] But the higher you go, the redder the room.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: When someone close beats you at something central to who you are, the closer they are, the bigger the threat to how you see yourself.
lines.say: [calm, careful, the fact said close] When someone close beats you at something central to who you are, the closer they are, the bigger the threat to how you see yourself.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: And his number keeps going down.
lines.say: [quiet, dread] And his number keeps going down.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Second place. An empty desk beside you. So what does first cost?
lines.say: [flat, then the question sharp] Second place. An empty desk beside you. So what does first cost?
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: The late-night study room. Past midnight. His seat's empty, and his notebook's open.
lines.say: [hushed, slow, a room with one lamp] The late-night study room. Past midnight. His seat's empty, and his notebook's open.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: You stopped helping him. He never stopped helping you.
lines.say: [quiet, the second sentence barely voiced] You stopped helping him. He never stopped helping you.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: He isn't sawing your chair. He's climbing.
lines.say: [soft, a realisation, the last word lifted] He isn't sawing your chair. He's climbing.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Envy comes in two kinds. One pushes you to move up. The other pushes you to pull the other person down.
lines.say: [calm, clear, the two kinds weighed] Envy comes in two kinds. One pushes you to move up. The other pushes you to pull the other person down.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Minus never meant they want you to fail. It meant it hurt.
lines.say: [slow, the planted line broken, the last word soft] Minus never meant they want you to fail. It meant it hurt.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: In one brain-scan study, envying a peer who did better at something that mattered came with activity in a region also active in pain.
lines.say: [measured, careful, landing on pain] In one brain-scan study, envying a peer who did better at something that mattered came with activity in a region also active in pain.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: A card has one colour for every kind of hurt.
lines.say: [quiet, complete, a line to keep] A card has one colour for every kind of hurt.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: But here's the second problem. Problem two: hurt needs a lane. Outside yours, nobody bleeds.
lines.say: [leaning in, hushed, certain] But here's the second problem. Problem two: hurt needs a lane. Outside yours, nobody bleeds.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: And you've only ever read one lane.
lines.say: [low, a door left open] And you've only ever read one lane.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Then a second letter from the school. The scholarship is confirmed: four years of university, fully paid. On one condition: top grades in the national exam, three weeks from now.
lines.say: [bright, building, then serious on the condition] Then a second letter from the school. The scholarship is confirmed: four years of university, fully paid. On one condition: top grades in the national exam, three weeks from now.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: For once you run home instead of to the store.
lines.say: [warm, running, glad] For once you run home instead of to the store.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Your sister's at the table. A night off. You say it to her face.
lines.say: [warm, then a held breath on the last sentence] Your sister's at the table. A night off. You say it to her face.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Ji-yoon: Say it again...
lines.say: Say it again...
lines.speaker: Ji-yoon

lines.text: Minus sixty-eight. Over the one person who ever asked to hear it twice.
lines.say: [hollow, slow, hurt] Minus sixty-eight. Over the one person who ever asked to hear it twice.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Ji-yoon: Say it again...
lines.say: Say it again...
lines.speaker: Ji-yoon

lines.text: You can't. You just watched a card say what her arms didn't.
lines.say: [quiet, flat, the second sentence slower] You can't. You just watched a card say what her arms didn't.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: You take your bag. And you don't go home. Not that night. Not for a month.
lines.say: [low, each sentence a door closing] You take your bag. And you don't go home. Not that night. Not for a month.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: A week in the study room. You say nothing good to anyone, so the cards go quiet.
lines.say: [hushed, tired, the quiet audible] A week in the study room. You say nothing good to anyone, so the cards go quiet.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: The night before the exam, you open your own notebook. Every mistake you made this year, and how you fixed it. The best study guide in your class.
lines.say: [quiet, slow, a lamp at night] The night before the exam, you open your own notebook. Every mistake you made this year, and how you fixed it. The best study guide in your class.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Give it to him, and he might pass you. Keep it, and first place stays yours.
lines.say: [low, weighing it, a beat between the two halves] Give it to him, and he might pass you. Keep it, and first place stays yours.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: You leave it on his desk, with half a chocolate bar on top. He did it for you first.
lines.say: [soft, sure, warm on the last sentence] You leave it on his desk, with half a chocolate bar on top. He did it for you first.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Exam morning. Outside every exam school, parents crowd the gate to see their kids in.
lines.say: [hushed, cold morning air, unhurried] Exam morning. Outside every exam school, parents crowd the gate to see their kids in.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: And there in the crowd, straight off the night shift, still in her work vest: your sister. With a lunch box.
lines.say: [tender, slowing, the last four words almost a smile] And there in the crowd, straight off the night shift, still in her work vest: your sister. With a lunch box.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Neither of you says a word. Nothing opens.
lines.say: [soft, the second sentence a relief and a loss] Neither of you says a word. Nothing opens.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: The gate closes behind you. And the whole country goes quiet.
lines.say: [hushed, slow, a held breath] The gate closes behind you. And the whole country goes quiet.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: It's true. In November 2025, during the English listening test, South Korea stopped its planes taking off and landing for 35 minutes, so their noise wouldn't disturb the students.
lines.say: [clear, plain, a little amazed] It's true. In November twenty twenty-five, during the English listening test, South Korea stopped its planes taking off and landing for thirty-five minutes, so their noise wouldn't disturb the students.

lines.text: This year, a country holds its breath for you.
lines.say: [quiet, slow, a lump in the throat] This year, a country holds its breath for you.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Results come in a month. For a month, you say nothing to anyone.
lines.say: [low, steady, time passing] Results come in a month. For a month, you say nothing to anyone.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Results. Top grade. Top grade. Top grade. The scholarship holds.
lines.say: [tight, then each grade a release, the last sentence exhaled] Results. Top grade. Top grade. Top grade. The scholarship holds.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Your best friend, beside you: top grade in maths too.
lines.say: [warm, surprised, glad] Your best friend, beside you: top grade in maths too.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Here's what you had backwards. You treated the four per cent like four places in a room. But in most subjects, it's the top 4 per cent of everyone in the country who sat it. His grade never cost you yours.
lines.say: [clear, a realisation unfolding, the last sentence quiet] Here's what you had backwards. You treated the four per cent like four places in a room. But in most subjects, it's the top four per cent of everyone in the country who sat it. His grade never cost you yours.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Min-jun: You want half?
lines.say: [bright, easy, clear, every night the same] You want half?
lines.speaker: Min-jun

lines.text: You take it.
lines.say: [soft, simple, a smile] You take it.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Your phone buzzes. Nine messages from the nine you cut. Nine congratulations. Not one card. A screen opens nothing.
lines.say: [quiet, a wince, the last sentence an echo of the rule] Your phone buzzes. Nine messages from the nine you cut. Nine congratulations. Not one card. A screen opens nothing.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: In studies of regret, the most common is education: about a third of all regrets.
lines.say: [calm, careful, the fact set down gently] In studies of regret, the most common is education: about a third of all regrets.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Her brushes have stood in a jar for six years.
lines.say: [soft, slow, the fact landing on her] Her brushes have stood in a jar for six years.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Text her, and never see her colour again. Or take the bus to the warehouse and say it to her face.
lines.say: [the dilemma, both halves fair, no pause after] Text her, and never see her colour again. Or take the bus to the warehouse and say it to her face.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: A text would open nothing. You could keep her forever on a screen.
lines.say: [quiet, the temptation honest] A text would open nothing. You could keep her forever on a screen.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: You're on the bus.
lines.say: [plain, decided, a breath of relief] You're on the bus.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Six o'clock. Her shift ends. You stand on the loading dock. And you say it.
lines.say: [steady, a held breath before the last sentence] Six o'clock. Her shift ends. You stand on the loading dock. And you say it.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Minus sixty-eight. The same.
lines.say: [flat, quiet, no surprise left] Minus sixty-eight. The same.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: She holds on. And this time you don't go stiff.
lines.say: [soft, warm, a change] She holds on. And this time you don't go stiff.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Ji-yoon: Say it again...
lines.say: [crying and laughing at once, into your shoulder, soft] Say it again.
lines.speaker: Ji-yoon

lines.text: You do.
lines.say: [barely voiced, certain] You do.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: The card gets two minutes. It doesn't get to choose what you do next.
lines.say: [low, steady, the second sentence firm] The card gets two minutes. It doesn't get to choose what you do next.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: You said nobody outside your lane bleeds.
lines.say: [quiet, turning the earlier line over] You said nobody outside your lane bleeds.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: She was never outside your lane. She was in it first.
lines.say: [slow, the turn, the last two words soft] She was never outside your lane. She was in it first.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Six years ago it was her letter on the fridge.
lines.say: [hushed, the picture landing] Six years ago it was her letter on the fridge.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: At the 1992 Summer Olympics, bronze medallists looked happier than silver. Silver thinks of the gold it nearly won. Bronze thinks of nearly winning nothing.
lines.say: [calm, exact, the last sentence slower] At the nineteen ninety-two Summer Olympics, bronze medallists looked happier than silver. Silver thinks of the gold it nearly won. Bronze thinks of nearly winning nothing.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: She's not watching you fail. She's watching the life she handed you walk up the dock with the news. And she wants it in.
lines.say: [warm, slow, the last sentence quiet but clear] She's not watching you fail. She's watching the life she handed you walk up the dock with the news. And she wants it in.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Morning. The fridge. She unpins the calendar, and behind it is a letter. Hers. Six years old.
lines.say: [quiet, morning light, slowing on the last two sentences] Morning. The fridge. She unpins the calendar, and behind it is a letter. Hers. Six years old.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: For once, silence leaves both of you in the room.
lines.say: [soft, settled] For once, silence leaves both of you in the room.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Tomorrow someone you love will pause half a second before they say congratulations.
lines.say: [close, gentle, slow] Tomorrow someone you love will pause half a second before they say congratulations.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: That half-second is the other life, going past.
lines.say: [hushed, complete, a line to keep] That half-second is the other life, going past.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Then the door. Your best friend. A letter of his own. He says it. For the first time, the good news isn't yours.
lines.say: [a lift of surprise, then the last sentence slow and uneasy] Then the door. Your best friend. A letter of his own. He says it. For the first time, the good news isn't yours.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Min-jun: I got in!
lines.say: [joyful, loud, clear] I got in!
lines.speaker: Min-jun

lines.text: Now it's his news. And the card is over you. Be honest: what number would open over your head? Tell us in the comments. And if you'd have done the same, hit like and subscribe.
lines.say: [quiet, direct, a small smile on be honest, unhurried] Now it's his news. And the card is over you. Be honest: what number would open over your head? Tell us in the comments. And if you'd have done the same, hit like and subscribe.
lines.speaker: narrator
